README.md.content:
# Linux lab identity and readiness

The report observes an existing Linux guest, WSL instance or owned remote lab.
It does not provision a VM, install packages, create users or change privilege
policy. A non-Linux host shell returns status 2 before reporting readiness.
The active identity comes from id, not a replaceable USER environment value.
The script interpreter and configured login shell are labeled separately.

## Provision one owned environment before reporting readiness

For a VM, use an already approved hypervisor and a dedicated new virtual disk.
A lab allocation of two virtual CPUs, 4 GB RAM and 32 GB disk leaves room for the
course. Download the Ubuntu Server installer matching the guest architecture
from Ubuntu, attach the ISO, select NAT networking and boot the new guest. Choose
language, keyboard and DHCP networking, then use only the new virtual disk for
the guided storage layout. Create an ordinary login account and a lab hostname,
complete installation, detach the ISO and reboot. Log in, record /etc/os-release
and uname -m, and take a named hypervisor snapshot before later changes. Shut
down, reopen the VM and confirm the same account and workspace are available.
These lab allocations are course choices, not claims about platform minimums.
The [Ubuntu installation guide](https://ubuntu.com/server/docs/tutorial/basic-installation/)
supports the installer sequence.

For Windows 11 or a supported Windows 10 build, open an administrator PowerShell
and run wsl --list --online. Choose the listed Ubuntu distribution intended for
the lab, then run wsl --install -d NAME, substituting that exact listed name.
Restart if requested, launch the distribution, and create its Linux account.
In PowerShell, wsl --list --verbose must show version 2; if it shows version 1,
use wsl --set-version NAME 2. Open the Linux distribution shell and record its
actual release before running course commands. The
[Microsoft WSL guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install)
supports these commands. Linux paths and Windows paths remain different.

An owned remote lab is another route: connect with its assigned SSH account,
record that host's identity and permitted scope, and obtain its snapshot/reset
method. A shared or production host is not a disposable course VM. The report
below verifies observations after provisioning; it cannot prove that the VM,
WSL distribution or reset route was created successfully.

## Run and interpret the observations

Extract one role and this guide. In the Linux lab, run:

~~~sh
bash lab_bootstrap_report.sh > readiness.txt 2> diagnostics.txt
report_status=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$report_status"
cat readiness.txt
cat /etc/os-release
ps -p 1 -o comm=
id
~~~

A successful report identifies the active account, kernel, working directory,
available commands and major filesystem locations. In the reference, WSL is
identified from the Linux proc version; systemd-detect-virt can identify another
virtualized context. The generic linux label states only that the kernel check
passed and a more specific context was not detected. Missing commands are
observations, not permission to install them on the host.

The starter's four TODO observations remain required: Linux context, course
workspace, package manager and privilege availability. Record distribution,
release, architecture, PID 1, identity, group membership, network boundary,
workspace and the VM's actual snapshot/reset route. An available sudo command
does not itself prove authorization for a later state change. Explain how the
workspace can be reopened and which later labs depend on missing tools.

## Walkthrough and independent evidence

Trace the early kernel guard before command inventory. Compare active identity
with configured shell information. Record a missing-tool case and the host-shell
failure separately from a healthy Linux report. The supplied course readiness
transcript is a clearly fictional reasoning route when a compatible Linux lab
is unavailable; it is not an observed VM. A successful script does not establish
that a VM was provisioned or complete the readiness record.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
[[ "$(uname -s)" == Linux ]] || { printf "Use the Linux guest or WSL shell; host identity is not Linux readiness.\n" >&2; exit 2; }

echo "== Linux Systems Lab Bootstrap Report =="
echo "Active identity: $(id -un) uid=$(id -u) groups=$(id -G)"
echo "Configured home environment: ${HOME:-unknown}"
echo "Script interpreter: Bash $BASH_VERSION"
echo "Configured login shell: ${SHELL:-unknown}"
echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"
echo "Kernel: $(uname -sr)"
echo "Working directory: $(pwd)"
echo

echo "== Command Check =="
for command_name in bash ls pwd grep find awk sed ssh systemctl journalctl crontab; do
	if command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "[ok] $command_name -> $(command -v "$command_name")"
	else
		echo "[missing] $command_name"
	fi
done
echo

echo "== TODO =="
echo "1. Confirm you are inside Linux, not a host shell."
echo "2. Create a course workspace under your home directory."
echo "3. Record which package manager this machine uses."
echo "4. Note whether you have sudo access."

solution/lab_bootstrap_report.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
[[ "$(uname -s)" == Linux ]] || { printf "Use the Linux guest or WSL shell; host identity is not Linux readiness.\n" >&2; exit 2; }

#################
#   CONSTANTS   #
#################
readonly -a PACKAGE_MANAGER_CANDIDATES=(apt dnf yum zypper pacman apk)
readonly -a COMMAND_CHECKS=(bash ls pwd grep find awk sed ssh systemctl journalctl crontab curl ip ss)
readonly -a PATH_CHECKS=(/ /home /etc /var /usr /tmp /srv)

#################
#   FUNCTIONS   #
#################
# Detect the first common package manager available on this system
detect_package_manager() {
	# Check each package manager candidate in the preferred reporting order
	for candidate in "${PACKAGE_MANAGER_CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
		# Report the first available package manager and stop searching
		if command -v "$candidate" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
			printf '%s' "$candidate"
			return 0
		fi
	done

	# Fall back when no known package manager is available
	printf 'unknown'
}

# Detect whether the lab is running under WSL, virtualization, or plain Linux
detect_linux_context() {
	# Prefer WSL detection because it also appears as Linux
	if grep -qi microsoft /proc/version 2>/dev/null; then
		printf 'wsl'
	# Report virtualized Linux when systemd exposes that information
	elif systemd-detect-virt --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
		printf 'virtualized-linux'
	# Use the generic Linux label for bare-metal or unknown environments
	else
		printf 'linux'
	fi
}

#################
#   MAIN CODE   #
#################
echo "== Linux Systems Lab Bootstrap Report =="
echo "Timestamp: $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
echo "Context: $(detect_linux_context)"
echo "Active identity: $(id -un) uid=$(id -u) groups=$(id -G)"
echo "Configured home environment: ${HOME:-unknown}"
echo "Script interpreter: Bash $BASH_VERSION"
echo "Configured login shell: ${SHELL:-unknown}"
echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"
echo "Kernel: $(uname -sr)"
echo "Package manager: $(detect_package_manager)"
echo "Working directory: $(pwd)"
echo

echo "== Command Check =="
for command_name in "${COMMAND_CHECKS[@]}"; do
	# Report whether each course command is available on PATH
	if command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "[ok] $command_name -> $(command -v "$command_name")"
	else
		echo "[missing] $command_name"
	fi
done
echo

echo "== Filesystem Orientation =="
for path_name in "${PATH_CHECKS[@]}"; do
	# Report whether each major filesystem location exists
	if [[ -e "$path_name" ]]; then
		printf '[ok] %s exists\n' "$path_name"
	else
		printf '[missing] %s\n' "$path_name"
	fi
done
echo

echo "== Next Actions =="
echo "1. Create ~/linux-systems-lab if it does not exist."
echo "2. Save this report to your course notebook."
echo "3. Record whether sudo is available with: sudo -v"

README.md.content:
# Shell foundations: trustworthy log summary

This project composes enumeration, quoting, structured filtering, aggregation,
diagnostics and exit status. It reads an immediate directory of regular .log
files. It does not rewrite the inputs or search subdirectories. A symbolic link
is not a regular input in this exercise. The timestamp is field one, the level
is field two, and the remaining text is the message. Only the exact levels ERROR
and WARNING contribute to their respective totals.

## Concepts and worked prediction

The directory contains three log files, including an empty file and a filename
with a space. app 1.log contains two errors and one warning; app-2.log contains
one error and one warning. An INFO message containing the word ERROR contributes
no error. notes.txt is excluded. The reference result is therefore:

~~~text
files=3 errors=3 warnings=2
~~~

find emits NUL-separated paths because a line is not a safe filename boundary.
The read loop uses the same separator and quotes each path. The manifest is
written before aggregation so an enumeration failure retains its failure
status. awk counts the level field and returns two numeric values even when a
file is empty. The totals are printed only after all selected inputs are read.
Diagnostics remain on standard error. Successful empty input is different from
an unreadable or missing directory.

## Open and run

Use a Linux lab with Bash, find, awk and mktemp. Extract the selected role folder
with its reports subdirectory, retaining this guide. From that folder:

~~~sh
bash task.sh
bash task.sh reports > summary.txt 2> diagnostics.txt
task_status=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$task_status"
cat summary.txt
cat diagnostics.txt
~~~

The relative default is anchored to the script location, so running the script
from another working directory selects the same supplied reports. An explicit
directory argument selects a changed case. A missing directory returns status
1 and no successful summary. An extra argument returns status 2.

## Learner work and independent checks

The starter already reads and counts the inputs, but deliberately discards the
warning count at the named TODO. Remove that defect without changing the error
count, input format or output format. Record the prediction before running it.
Create a separate empty directory, a directory with one matching line, and a
directory with multiple matching lines. Add an INFO message containing ERROR,
a non-log text file and a filename containing spaces. Record summary, diagnostic
output and status for each case. Test a missing directory as a failure case.
Compare the reference only after recording a working attempt.

## Instructor walkthrough and completion evidence

Walk the supplied paths through find, the NUL read loop and awk before running
the complete pipeline. Explain why grep with an unconditional 'or true' cannot
distinguish no matches from an input error. Completion requires the named TODO
repair, the changed-case record and an explanation of the status boundary;
running a supplied program does not complete that reasoning record.

starter/task.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
readonly SCRIPT_DIR
input_dir="${1:-$SCRIPT_DIR/reports}"
[[ $# -le 1 ]] || { printf 'Usage: bash task.sh [log-directory]\n' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -d "$input_dir" && -r "$input_dir" && -x "$input_dir" ]] || {
    printf 'Cannot inspect log directory: %s\n' "$input_dir" >&2; exit 1;
}
input_dir="$(cd -- "$input_dir" && pwd -P)"
manifest="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f -- "$manifest"' EXIT
# Save enumeration first so a failed find cannot become a successful summary.
find "$input_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.log' -print0 > "$manifest"
file_count=0
error_total=0
warning_total=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' log_path; do
    # The second whitespace-separated field is the level, not a message word.
    counts="$(awk '$2 == "ERROR" {e++} $2 == "WARNING" {w++} END {print e+0, w+0}' "$log_path")"
    read -r error_count warning_count <<< "$counts"
    warning_count=0 # TODO: retain the warning count returned by awk.
    ((file_count+=1))
    ((error_total+=error_count)) || true
    ((warning_total+=warning_count)) || true
done < "$manifest"
printf 'files=%s errors=%s warnings=%s\n' "$file_count" "$error_total" "$warning_total"

# Static content under /srv: publish and verify exact state

The page installer accepts an explicit document root inside the owned Linux lab.
It anchors source index.html to the script's directory, not the working directory.
No system Nginx configuration is changed by the script. The starter's named TODO
is deliberately unfinished; the reference installs the neighboring page with
0644 mode, applies requested ownership, then publishes it. Ownership errors are
fatal and retain an earlier page. Ownership changes target only the document
root and staged page, never a recursive tree of unrelated files.

## Independent filesystem run

Extract one role with index.html and the configuration. In Linux:

~~~sh
lab_root=$(mktemp -d)
bash deploy_static_site.sh "$lab_root/public"
stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' "$lab_root/public" "$lab_root/public/index.html"
cmp index.html "$lab_root/public/index.html"
~~~

The root is 0755 and the page is 0644. Omitting owner preserves the active
account's ownership; an explicit OWNER:GROUP must be applied successfully.
Repeat from another working directory, with spaces in the target path, and with
an invalid owner. For the failure case, create an earlier known page and verify
its bytes remain unchanged. Record output, diagnostics and status. Complete the
starter TODO without replacing its ownership/error boundary.

## Owned VM Nginx route

The supplied server block listens only on 127.0.0.1:8080 and has no default_server
claim. This avoids conflict with the distribution's ordinary default site and
does not create a public listener. In the disposable VM, publish to
/srv/linux-systems-site, using its intended serving owner when administrative
permission is available. Inspect the exact source and target paths before a
privileged command. Copy the reviewed block into the VM's sites-available folder
and enable only its named symlink in sites-enabled. Validate with nginx -t before
reloading the VM's Nginx service. Request http://127.0.0.1:8080/ from that VM,
compare the served page, and request an unknown path to verify status 404.

For a temporary document root, replace only the root directive with the exact
published absolute path before enabling that block. Each parent directory must
allow the Nginx worker identity to traverse it; a default private mktemp parent
does not grant that traversal. Use the owned /srv route or an explicitly planned
lab layout rather than opening unrelated home directories recursively.

Record the account, directory modes, syntax-test result, reload result, served
bytes and unknown-path status independently. A successful copy does not prove
that Nginx is serving that path. Preserve the prior VM configuration and disable
only the named lab site to undo it; validate before the restoration reload.
Completion includes the TODO, changed cases, serving observations and an undo.

starter/deploy_static_site.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
[[ "$(uname -s)" == Linux ]] || { printf 'This deployment lab requires Linux.\n' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $# -ge 1 && $# -le 2 ]] || { printf 'Usage: bash deploy_static_site.sh SITE_ROOT [OWNER:GROUP]\n' >&2; exit 2; }
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
readonly SCRIPT_DIR
site_root="$1"
site_owner="${2:-}"
[[ ! -L "$site_root" ]] || { printf 'The document root cannot be a symlink.\n' >&2; exit 2; }
mkdir -p -- "$site_root"
site_root="$(cd -- "$site_root" && pwd -P)"
temporary="$(mktemp "$site_root/.index-pending-XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f -- "$temporary"' EXIT
install_page() {
    [[ -n "$1" && -n "$2" ]] || return 2
    return 1 # TODO: install source argument 1 into staged argument 2 with mode 0644.
}
install_page "$SCRIPT_DIR/index.html" "$temporary"
# Ownership failure is fatal and occurs before replacing an earlier page.
if [[ -n "$site_owner" ]]; then
    chown -- "$site_owner" "$temporary"
    chown -- "$site_owner" "$site_root"
fi
chmod 0755 -- "$site_root"
mv -f -- "$temporary" "$site_root/index.html"
printf 'Published %s/index.html\n' "$site_root"
stat -c 'mode=%a uid=%u gid=%g path=%n' -- "$site_root" "$site_root/index.html"
printf 'Set the Nginx root to that exact path, validate configuration, then request the lab listener at http://127.0.0.1:8080/.\n'

README.md.content:
# Users, groups and permissions: diagnose ancestor traversal

This Linux project creates one bounded directory tree under an empty directory
owned by an unprivileged account. It changes no system accounts, supplementary
groups or unrelated paths. Running as root is rejected because root can bypass
the access failure this lesson observes.

## Permission model

Each mode has owner, group and other classes. Read on a regular file permits
reading its bytes; write permits modifying bytes. Directory read permits
listing names, execute permits traversal and access to named children, and
write plus execute permits creating or removing directory entries. Deleting a
file is principally a permission on its containing directory, not its file
write bit. Effective group membership includes supplementary groups.

The supplied file is 0640 and belongs to the active account. Its private parent
is 0600: the same owner has read and write on the directory, but no traversal.
The file remains unreadable through that path. Adding owner execute to that
parent repairs access without broadening group or other permissions.

## Create, inspect and correct the owned lab

Extract one role and the guide. In an unprivileged Linux shell:

~~~sh
lab_root=$(mktemp -d)
bash task.sh setup "$lab_root"
bash task.sh inspect "$lab_root"
bash task.sh fix "$lab_root"
bash task.sh verify "$lab_root"
~~~

Setup prints can_read=no. Before the correction, verify returns status 1.
The reference fix prints can_read=yes; final verify confirms parent mode 0700
and unchanged file mode 0640. The starter fix is deliberately unfinished at
the named TODO. Replace it with one targeted command. Record the predicted and
observed results in permissions.md before comparing the reference.

To undo the correction inside this lab, set only the private parent back to
0600 and repeat inspect. To remove the disposable tree, first restore owner
traversal with the completed fix, verify the recorded lab_root value, then
remove exactly that directory. Setup refuses nonempty directories and later
operations require the owned marker and nonsymlink directory layout.

## Supplied service-identity case

The following case is fictional; the program's physical observations do not
prove access for other accounts. Predict it from identities and complete paths:

~~~text
0750 root:signal-web /srv/signal-garden
2750 deploy:signal-web /srv/signal-garden/releases
0640 deploy:signal-web /srv/signal-garden/releases/index.html
deploy and www-data belong to signal-web; observer does not.
~~~

deploy can traverse, read and write the file, and create or remove entries in
releases. www-data can traverse and read, but cannot write the file or change
directory entries. observer cannot traverse the first directory. A shared
group does not automatically grant write permission; the mode bits govern it.
The setgid bit on releases makes newly created entries inherit its group,
subject to the actual creation mode and umask.

## Walkthrough and completion evidence

Explain the owner/group/other selection before each observation. Locate the
first failed ancestor instead of recursively changing permissions. Completion
requires the TODO repair, the independent record, the supplied identity matrix
and an observed undo. A successful reference program does not complete the
worksheet or establish access for the fictional service accounts.

README.md.content:
# Backups, cron and a user timer

This Linux lab archives an explicit source directory into a separate owned
backup directory. Both scheduler examples use the same unprivileged account
and explicit paths. The systemd files are user units, not system units: installing
them with a system-wide manager would select the wrong identity and home.

## Archive and retention contract

Run Bash with GNU find, sort, tar, mktemp, realpath and the util-linux flock command.
Source and destination may contain spaces. The destination must be outside the
source tree. RETENTION_COUNT is a canonical integer from 1 through 1000; zero
and malformed values are rejected before an archive is created. The default is
five. Managed archive names begin with linux-systems-backup- and end in .tar.gz;
reserve that naming convention for this lab. Other files and symlinks are not
selected for retention.

Each successful run creates a new timestamped name with a unique suffix. A lock
serializes runs sharing a destination. tar writes a temporary archive and only
then publishes it without replacing any existing archive. A failed creation
removes temporary files and leaves earlier backups intact. The reference keeps
the archive just created plus the newest remaining managed archives, up to the
retention count. Retention failure is an error, not a success report. Archive
members are relative to the source, so restoration can target a separate tree.

## First run and independent restoration

Use a disposable Linux workspace containing fabricated course files:

~~~sh
lab_root=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$lab_root/source notes" "$lab_root/backup copies" "$lab_root/restored"
printf 'first observation\n' > "$lab_root/source notes/session.txt"
bash backup_home.sh "$lab_root/source notes" "$lab_root/backup copies"
find "$lab_root/backup copies" -name 'linux-systems-backup-*.tar.gz' -print
~~~

Select the archive path printed by the program. List its members with tar -tzf,
then extract this known lab archive with tar -xzf into the separate restored
directory. Compare session.txt against the original with cmp. Record the archive
name, input, restored bytes, status and any diagnostics. Archive creation alone
does not prove restoration.

The starter creates correct, unique archives but its named retention TODO is
unfinished. Complete that one operation without replacing the input contract,
lock or publication sequence. Make seven backups with changed content and
RETENTION_COUNT=2, then verify two managed archives remain and the newest
restores the newest input. Repeat with retention one, an unrelated file, a
missing source, zero retention and paths containing spaces. Earlier backups
remain unchanged when creation fails. Compare the reference after an attempted
repair and independent restore.

## Install the selected role for a user scheduler

In the owned Linux lab, create the source and backup directories and install
the selected completed script. These commands do not configure a system service:

~~~sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" "$HOME/linux-systems-lab" "$HOME/backups"
install -m 0755 backup_home.sh "$HOME/.local/bin/backup_home.sh"
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/systemd/user"
install -m 0644 linux-backup.service linux-backup.timer "$HOME/.config/systemd/user/"
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user start linux-backup.service
systemctl --user status linux-backup.service
journalctl --user -u linux-backup.service --no-pager
systemctl --user enable --now linux-backup.timer
systemctl --user list-timers
~~~

The %h specifier expands to the user manager's home. No root HOME default is
used. A user manager may require an active login session; record actual manager
availability and behavior rather than assuming it exists in every VM or WSL
session. If unavailable, use the manual run and supplied unit reasoning route.
For cron, inspect the existing user crontab first and add only the one example
entry. Do not replace an existing crontab wholesale. The example sets a known
shell and PATH and uses explicit source and destination arguments. Test one
scheduler at a time; the destination lock also prevents overlapping archive
publication. Verify actual scheduled output and restoration.

## Undo and completion evidence

Disable and stop the named user timer, then remove only the two installed lab
unit files and run user daemon-reload. Remove only the added cron line if it was
used. Retain earlier backups until the independent restore has been verified.
Completion includes the retention TODO, changed cases, an actual restoration,
the scheduler identity/path record and a tested undo. A program run does not
prove worksheet completion or that a timer executed.

starter/backup_home.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
[[ "$(uname -s)" == Linux ]] || { printf 'This backup lab requires Linux tools.\n' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $# == 2 ]] || { printf 'Usage: bash backup_home.sh SOURCE_DIRECTORY BACKUP_DIRECTORY\n' >&2; exit 2; }
source_dir="$1"
dest_dir="$2"
retention_count="${RETENTION_COUNT:-5}"
[[ "$retention_count" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$ && "$retention_count" -le 1000 ]] || { printf 'RETENTION_COUNT must be an integer from 1 through 1000.\n' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -d "$source_dir" ]] || { printf 'Missing source directory.\n' >&2; exit 2; }
source_dir="$(cd -- "$source_dir" && pwd -P)"
[[ "$source_dir" != / ]] || { printf 'Select an owned lab source, not the filesystem root.\n' >&2; exit 2; }
dest_dir="$(realpath -m -- "$dest_dir")"
case "$dest_dir/" in "$source_dir/"*) printf 'The backup directory must be outside the source tree.\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
umask 077
mkdir -p -- "$dest_dir"
dest_dir="$(cd -- "$dest_dir" && pwd -P)"
case "$dest_dir/" in "$source_dir/"*) printf 'The backup directory must be outside the source tree.\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
umask 077
exec 9> "$dest_dir/.linux-systems-backup.lock"
flock -x -w 30 9 || { printf 'Backup lock is busy.\n' >&2; exit 1; }
temporary="$(mktemp "$dest_dir/.backup-XXXXXX")"
inventory="$(mktemp "$dest_dir/.retention-XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f -- "$temporary" "$inventory"' EXIT
stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
temporary_name="${temporary##*/}"
suffix="${temporary_name#.backup-}"
archive_name="linux-systems-backup-$stamp-$suffix.tar.gz"
# Relative archive members permit restoration into a separate owned directory.
tar -C "$source_dir" -czf "$temporary" .
# Hard-link publication refuses replacement of an existing archive name.
ln -- "$temporary" "$dest_dir/$archive_name"
rm -f -- "$temporary"
# Keep the archive just created, plus the newest retention_count - 1 older ones.
find "$dest_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'linux-systems-backup-*.tar.gz' ! -name "$archive_name" -printf '%T@ %f\0' > "$inventory"
LC_ALL=C sort -z -nr -o "$inventory" "$inventory"
kept=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' record; do
    old_name="${record#* }"
    : "$old_name" # TODO: remove older managed archives once kept reaches retention_count - 1.
    ((kept+=1))
done < "$inventory"
printf 'Created %s\n' "$dest_dir/$archive_name"

README.md.content:
# Run an application behind Nginx

This lab distinguishes the application socket, the front-end proxy socket and
the source of an HTTP response. Use Python 3, Nginx, curl and ss in an owned Linux
lab. The app and proxy listen only on loopback high ports. The supplied unit is
an optional user service, with the same ordinary account as the manual route.
Neither source program installs software or changes a system-wide site.

## Request contract and prediction

Both roles implement GET and HEAD /health: status 200 with service linux-toy-app
and status ok. Unknown paths return JSON 404. POST returns JSON 405 with Allow:
GET, HEAD. The request target is limited to 4096 characters and at most 16 query
fields; excessive query fields return JSON 400. Content-Length counts UTF-8
bytes, including the response newline; HEAD has the same headers without a body.
APP_PORT is a canonical ASCII integer from 1024 through 65535. Invalid settings
exit 2 before binding; an occupied port exits 1. The default app port is 8081.

GET /inspect records the actual path, parsed query, transport peer and four
received headers. Repeated query keys remain lists and blank values remain
visible. For /inspect?mode=read&mode=write&blank=, predict a path of /inspect,
a two-element mode list and a one-element blank list containing an empty string.
The reference returns these observations. The starter deliberately returns
JSON 501 at the named TODO; health is not proof that inspection is complete.
Complete inspection_payload using its supplied arguments before comparing the
reference. Do not replace observations with fixed sample answers.

## Verify the application first

Extract one role and this guide. Confirm uname -s, id and the permitted host
scope. Check that ports 8081 and 8080 are free with ss -ltnp. If they are occupied,
choose two free high ports and change APP_PORT, proxy_pass and listen together.
From the selected role, keep this process running in its own terminal:

~~~sh
APP_PORT=8081 python3 app.py
~~~

In a second terminal, record status, headers and body for these direct requests:

~~~sh
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8081/health
curl -i 'http://127.0.0.1:8081/inspect?mode=read&mode=write&blank='
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8081/missing
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8081/health
ss -ltnp 'sport = :8081'
~~~

The startup line is flushed immediately. Record the actual PID and socket
identity. A process listing alone does not establish healthy HTTP behavior.
The app reports header values as data; a client can supply forwarding headers
directly. They are not authenticated identity or privilege evidence.

## Run the selected Nginx block in a disposable prefix

From the selected role, use this separate owned prefix. Keep the printed
lab_root value for every later command. The heredoc expands only the selected
absolute include path; the supplied proxy block keeps its Nginx variables.

~~~sh
lab_root=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$lab_root/logs"
install -m 0644 linux-toy-app.conf "$lab_root/proxy.conf"
cat > "$lab_root/nginx.conf" <<EOF
pid logs/nginx.pid;
error_log logs/main-error.log info;
events {}
http {
    access_log logs/main-access.log;
    include "$lab_root/proxy.conf";
}
EOF
nginx -p "$lab_root/" -c "$lab_root/nginx.conf" -t
nginx -p "$lab_root/" -c "$lab_root/nginx.conf" -g 'daemon off;'
~~~

Keep that Nginx process running in its terminal. In the request terminal:

~~~sh
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
curl -i 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/inspect?mode=read&mode=write&blank='
curl -i -H 'Host: lab.invalid' -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9' -H 'X-Forwarded-Proto: https' 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/inspect?topic=ports'
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/missing
ss -ltnp 'sport = :8080'
tail -n 10 "$lab_root/logs/proxy-access.log"
tail -n 10 "$lab_root/logs/proxy-error.log"
~~~

The two sockets are distinct. Without an added URI in proxy_pass, this block
forwards the request path and query. The app's unknown-path 404 and the starter's
unfinished 501 remain those statuses through the proxy. Nginx overwrites the
supplied forwarding headers with its observed loopback client and http scheme;
the supplied spoofed values do not become authentication evidence. Compare
Host and received forwarding headers against the direct request. The access
log records request, status and upstream attempt; a log field alone does not
prove that an app answered.

Stop the owned app with Ctrl-C while leaving the owned proxy running. A direct
health request now fails to connect and a proxied health request returns 502.
Read the proxy error log, restore the same app and verify recovery to 200.
This distinguishes an unavailable upstream from an app-produced 404 or 501.
A syntax test only validates configuration; it neither starts Nginx nor proves
that the intended socket or application is serving.

## Optional user-service route after foreground verification

Stop the foreground app before starting the same app port under a user manager.
The following route requires an available systemd user manager in the owned lab:

~~~sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/linux-toy-app" "$HOME/.config/systemd/user"
install -m 0644 app.py "$HOME/.local/share/linux-toy-app/app.py"
install -m 0644 linux-toy-app.service "$HOME/.config/systemd/user/"
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user start linux-toy-app.service
systemctl --user status linux-toy-app.service
journalctl --user -u linux-toy-app.service --no-pager
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8081/health
~~~

The unit uses the user manager's home and active account, not www-data or a root
HOME default. It needs no system-wide unit or /opt installation. Record actual
manager availability and inspect its working directory, environment and PID.
If the user bus is unavailable, retain the verified foreground route and record
that limitation; a parsed unit file is not an operating service. Restore any
pre-existing file before installing this lab under its name. The separate
Services and systemd project covers sustained service-operation evidence.

## Undo and completion record

Stop only the two foreground processes with Ctrl-C in their own terminals.
For the optional route, stop the named user service, restore or remove only its
lab unit and app file, and reload the user manager. Confirm the two lab sockets
are gone before removing the disposable prefix; preserve the logs until the
failure and recovery record is complete. No distribution default site is enabled,
replaced or claimed by this block.

Completion includes the inspection TODO repair, independent predictions and
observations, path/query and header comparisons, socket/PID evidence, the
upstream-down 502 and recovery, and a verified undo. A reference run does not
complete the record or establish public hosting or service-manager operation.

Primary references: [Python HTTP server](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/http.server.html)
and [Nginx proxy directives](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html).
